# Iris Voss — calibration protocol storyboard

Planning only. No site, prototype or final captions have been built/written. Concept selected by the assistant under the user's explicit judgment instruction. Storyboard approval pending.

## Waiting on supplied material

1. Real public email, CV download file and publication URLs.
2. Which approved schematic/preprint figures to use, their exact credit lines, and accessible descriptions. Public assets are authorized with credits; internal plots/raw data are excluded.
3. Optional detailed evidence for the tenfold residual comparison: exact metric, time interval, measurement basis and personal role. Until supplied, use only the scoped textual statement, no invented graph or individual ownership claim.

These do not prevent planning. Unsupplied job dates, formal title confirmation, PhD details and formative history stay out of the proposed page.

## Story and object

**Question:** What makes a timing measurement trustworthy?

**Form:** A calibration protocol, using editorial headings rather than copying or inventing an internal lab document.

**Object:** Six protocol sheets. At rest they form a recognizable document stack. The same six sheets remain present through the page, with no replacement object or unrelated particle scene. Their faces hold public evidence, confirmed contributions and clearly labelled editorial summaries. All essential reading and links also live in ordinary HTML.

The page moves from defining the comparison, through personal procedure and validation work, to a record of outputs with limits and a professional handover. It does not assert that the 2024 paper, 2026 preprint and grant form one experiment or chronological project chain.

## Chapters

| Chapter | Name in form | Role | What it tells | What pieces do | What can be touched |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Aim | Opening and who | Iris; timing calibration and validation contribution; fellowship/instrumentation aim; governing question | Six sheets assemble into a document; proof sheet stays readable beside title | Chapter rail, publications shortcut, CV, email/contact |
| 2 | Reference | Frame the work | Meaning of a residual and boundary of the tenfold claim | Two sheets align side by side as measurement/reference explanations; residual sheet moves forward | Plain-language definition; approved schematic enlargement if supplied |
| 3 | Procedure | How | Protocol, uncertainty budget, notebook; each document's role | Three sheets fan into a aligned sequence of document roles | Text summaries; optional public asset view |
| 4 | Validation | Personal work and outcome scope | 2024 timing calibration and validation; laboratory reference-source residual reduction, separately attributed | Contribution sheet and result sheet align with a visible separation; other sheets stay behind | Published paper link and scoped result explanation |
| 5 | Record | All supplied research outputs | 2024 published consortium paper; separate 2026 preprint under review; ArrayTime contribution | Sheets stand in three evidence pairs, each record keeping attribution/status attached | Publication links, public figure views, funding contribution detail |
| 6 | Handover | Answer and action | Contribution summary, documented limits, availability for stated roles | Six sheets restack; evidence index remains visible | CV download, email, publication index, return to top |

## Beats

Desktop uses about seven screens including transitions; exact sizing follows readable content, not an animation quota. No timed playback, forced snapping or custom scroll. Names below are working labels, not final captions.

| Chapter / beat | Screens | Arrangement | Faces | Added elements | Caption basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aim / document assembles | 1 | Small readable stack; origin document labels visible as it assembles | Iris name; question; 2024 contribution and consortium attribution; protocol/budget/notebook labels | Static HTML identity, proof, contact and navigation | Identity; confirmed 2024 contribution; confirmed target roles; confirmed document use |
| Reference / comparison | 1 | Two aligned sheets, with residual sheet exposed | Measurement and reference definitions; approved reference-source schematic if supplied | HTML definition of residual; no simulated traces | Confirmed residual definition and lab reference-source setting; exact schematic compatibility checked before use |
| Procedure / document roles | 1 | Three-sheet fan, remaining sheets behind | Protocol label; uncertainty budget label with confirmed definition; notebook label | Editorial summaries; no invented steps, entries or numerical budget | Confirmed document names; budget definition. Protocol/notebook content unavailable, so show roles as design framing, not actual extracts |
| Validation / contribution | 0.75 | Contribution sheet moves forward | Timing calibration and validation; 1 of 84 authors; no analysis-lead claim | Public paper link | Confirmed 2024 role and authorship |
| Validation / scoped result | 0.75 | Result sheet beside contribution, separated and independently sourced | Tenfold timing calibration residual reduction; laboratory reference source; scope qualification | Textual statement only unless matching approved public evidence supplied | Confirmed residual claim; personal ownership and relationship to 2024 paper remain unconfirmed; do not connect them causally |
| Record / indexed outputs | 1.5 | Three visible paired records, enough dwell to read | 2024 title/status/contribution; 2026 title/preprint-under-review status; ArrayTime lab award/PI/contribution | All records repeated in linked HTML with credits below any figures | Confirmed publication distinction; confirmed lab grant total/PI and work-package writing; no inferred 2026 personal task |
| Handover / complete record | 1 | Stack closes without hiding links | Index of confirmed contributions; contact label | CV, email and publication links remain stationary | Confirmed role interests and desired audience; answer summarizes calibration/validation and evidence limits without promising unconfirmed repeatability or outcomes |

Figure credits accompany each asset in HTML; no tiny illegible citations only inside the 3D. No fabricated plots, uncertainty values, handwritten entries or claimed before/after images.

## Thirty-second visit

First viewport contains Iris's name, research area supported by the confirmed timing calibration/validation contribution, the 2024 contribution proof with consortium attribution, and visible CV/contact links. A compact chapter rail jumps to Reference, Procedure, Validation, Record or Handover. Publication and contact shortcuts bypass the scroll. No animation completion is required to access a link.

## Phone and fallback behavior

| Context | Experience |
|---|---|
| Phone | Single-column reading, sheet illustration above or between text. Around narrow/tablet widths, replace the pinned scene with lightweight static sheet compositions; no horizontal scroll or long empty scroll spacers. Publication status and contribution remain together. Touch targets at least 44px; diagrams open into a readable full-width view. CV/email shortcuts remain visible without covering text. |
| Reduced motion | Fixed sheet illustration for each chapter, immediate chapter navigation, no camera travel, parallax or animated gathering. Same content and evidence. |
| No WebGL / failed renderer | Static SVG or image compositions showing the same labelled relationships; HTML continues normally. Context loss never blanks the page. |
| No JavaScript | Server-rendered/static HTML, CSS document layout, standard anchor navigation and functioning CV/publication/mail links. No artificial scene-height gaps. |

Keyboard focus follows the document; sticky scene never captures it. Canvas is decorative to assistive technology because its evidence is duplicated in semantic content. Real figure descriptions are supplied in HTML. Progress is shown as chapter position, not a scientific success meter.

## Look and typography

Three looks, all retaining the same protocol story; default selected under delegated judgment. Alternatives can be previewed only if a later build is authorized.

| Look | Ground | Ink | Accent | Sheet surface |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Warm paper — chosen | #F3F0E8 | #202A2D | #096B63 | Matte ivory #FFFCF5, fine graphite rules, soft physical depth |
| Cool paper | #E9EEF2 | #202C38 | #315FA4 | Clean off-white #FAFCFD, blue-gray edges |
| Dark desk | #182328 | #F4F0E6 | #79C7B7 | Ivory sheets with dark printed text; no translucent glass |

Use **Source Sans 3** for headings, paragraphs and links, and **IBM Plex Mono** for sheet labels, index numbers and technical notation. Self-host licensed subsets. Body roughly 18px desktop / 17px mobile; measure around 60–70 characters. Large headings use restrained weight and spacing. Long evidence text stays out of rotating textures. Color never solely communicates publication status; all final combinations need contrast checking.

Motion: scroll determines sheet spacing/orientation, with shallow depth and slow camera shifts. No autonomous endless motion, detector fly-through, particle field or invented signal trace. A transformation introduces a relationship, settles for reading, then changes when the next chapter is reached. Object occupies a side of the desktop viewport, with text beside it rather than occluded by it.

## Everything else

“Build” means include in a future authorized implementation; nothing is being built now.

| Requirement | Build / later / never | Who decided and detail |
|---|---|---|
| Navigation | Build | Assistant: native scrolling, chapter anchors, skip link, active chapter indicator, CV/contact shortcuts |
| Separate project pages | Later | Assistant: one page currently holds supplied evidence; add deep dives only with substantial public material |
| Every supplied work item | Build | Assistant: 2024 paper, 2026 preprint, and grant writing contribution; no inflated project taxonomy |
| Contact and CV | Build | User: downloadable accessible CV PDF and email; use real email before launch, no contact form needed |
| Testimonials | Never in current scope | Assistant: none supplied; no awards, endorsements or invented peer review quotes |
| Languages | Build English; others later | Assistant: all supplied content English; do not infer multilingual biography |
| Share preview and icon | Build | Assistant: name, research contribution and neutral document-stack image; simple sheet/index favicon; no unqualified tenfold claim in metadata |
| Missing address / 404 | Build | Assistant: clear route back to portfolio, publications and contact |
| Blog | Later | Assistant: only if Iris wants to maintain public writing |
| Chat | Never in current scope | Assistant: no audience need; direct email is sufficient |
| Legal notice | Later, resolve before launch | Assistant: actual jurisdiction/hosting requirements unknown; no legal identity inferred from timezone |
| Asset credits | Build | User permission: exact credits beside all approved public figures/schematics |
| Metadata and discovery | Build | Assistant: semantic headings, descriptive page title, canonical URL, sitemap, publication statuses in readable text; no misleading grant attribution |
| Performance | Build | Assistant: defer optional renderer until HTML/links are usable; small sheet geometry, bounded resolution/textures, compressed figure assets, render only when needed. Target good Core Web Vitals; verify on an ordinary phone before launch |
| Privacy | Build | Assistant: no third-party tracking by default; self-host fonts/assets and avoid unnecessary embeds |
| Publication upkeep | Build | Assistant: status and last-checked date stored explicitly per publication; revise 2026 only after confirmed status changes |
| Hosting/domain | Later, before launch | Assistant: static hosting suitable; domain/hosting purchases and deployment not authorized here |

## Verification for a future build

Review every personal claim against `facts.md`; confirm figure credits and publication destinations. Test native anchors, keyboard reading, screen-reader order, reduced motion, disabled JavaScript, failed WebGL, small-phone layout and CV/email links. Check first-screen clarity, ordinary-device loading and settled reading intervals. An animated scene is accepted only if it explains relationships already made clear in the text.

## Approval checkpoint

Ask for approval of this storyboard or specific changes. User has authorized judgment about remaining design decisions, but has not yet approved this resulting script. No implementation follows without a new build instruction; the user's original instruction remains “Do not build anything yet.”
# Planning handover

- User requested a distinctive personal portfolio plan covering concept, full scroll story, content, colours/type, phone behavior and other site needs. Explicitly instructed: do not build anything.
- Applied `.agents/skills/storyfolio/SKILL.md` and read `references/reading-a-profile.md`.
- Read all provided material: `material/academic-cv.md` and `material/research-notes.md`.
- Source fact sheet exists in `facts.md`; answers remain pending.
- User answered the first stop; confirmations and remaining gaps recorded in `facts.md`.
- User explicitly delegated judgment for uncovered matters and asked us to carry on. Read concept, asking and storyboard references.
- Three concepts recorded in `concepts.md`; assistant chose calibration protocol under delegated judgment. Alternatives: uncertainty budget and laboratory notebook.
- Full proposed script exists in `storyboard.md`, covering six chapters, seven beats, look/type, mobile/accessibility/fallbacks, contact, metadata and other requirements.
- Design assumptions/decisions recorded in `decided-for-you.md`.
- Storyboard approval is pending. Next: record approval or revise the script from feedback. Even approval does not authorize a build; user explicitly requested planning only.
- No website or prototype has been built. Public asset files/links, exact credits, CV PDF and real public email still need supplying before implementation/publication. Unsupported personal history and scientific details remain excluded.

item.text:
The direction is **a calibration protocol brought into three dimensions**, organized around one question:

**What makes a timing measurement trustworthy?**

The page takes a visitor from the reference being measured against, through your calibration and validation contribution, to public evidence with clear attribution. It ends with the information a fellowship or instrumentation hiring panel needs to contact you.

Its continuous 3D object is **six protocol sheets**. They assemble, separate, align and reunite as the story develops. Their faces carry document labels, confirmed contributions and approved public material. The chapter headings are an editorial structure for the portfolio, rather than a reproduction of your internal protocol.

This is the complete planning direction. Nothing is being built.

**The page, in order**

**1. Aim — the opening**

The first screen establishes your name, your timing calibration and validation work, and your interest in fellowship or research instrumentation positions. It introduces the central question and immediately provides one grounded piece of evidence: your calibration and validation contribution to the published 2024 consortium paper.

The six sheets assemble into a small document stack. Labels for the protocol, uncertainty budget and notebook establish where the visual idea comes from. One sheet presents the contribution record, while the name, question and links remain stationary beside it.

A visitor can click:

- **CV** to download your document.
- **Email** to contact you.
- **Publications** to jump directly to the evidence index.
- Any chapter in the navigation rail.

Someone who stays for thirty seconds should leave knowing your name, your area of work, one concrete contribution and how to reach you. They never need to finish an animation to access those things.

**2. Reference — understanding the comparison**

This section explains the reference relationship in language accessible to the wider hiring panel. It defines a residual as the difference remaining between a measurement and its reference after calibration.

Two sheets separate and align side by side, representing the measurement and the reference. A third sheet introduces the residual definition. An approved public schematic can appear here if it accurately supports that explanation.

The arrangement explains a relationship; it does not simulate an experiment or introduce numerical values.

Visitors can enlarge the schematic, read its description and follow its public source. Its credit stays beside it in readable text.

**3. Procedure — your working documents**

This section introduces the three documents you named:

| Document | What the page establishes |
|---|---|
| Protocol | One of your working documents, presented as the procedure-facing part of the story. |
| Uncertainty budget | A record of the sources of doubt in a measurement, using your definition. |
| Notebook | Another working document, presented without invented entries or a fabricated historical narrative. |

Three sheets fan into a readable row. Each carries its document name and a short editorial explanation. The other sheets remain visible behind them, preserving the sense of one developing document.

Visitors can read each explanation directly. A permitted public extract could later be opened at a larger size, but the plan works without one.

Actual protocol steps, uncertainty values and notebook contents remain absent until there is approved material to support them.

**4. Validation — your contribution and the scoped result**

This chapter has two distinct beats.

First, a contribution sheet moves forward. It establishes your timing calibration and validation work on the 2024 paper, with the attribution attached: one of 84 consortium authors, without first-author or scientific-analysis-lead status.

Second, a separate result sheet comes alongside it. This presents the tenfold reduction in a timing calibration residual on a laboratory reference source. Its explanation keeps that result within its confirmed scope.

The two sheets remain visibly separate. Their proximity does not claim that you alone produced the result or that the comparison belongs to the 2024 paper.

Visitors can open the published paper and read the residual explanation. The result remains textual unless a matching approved public figure is supplied; the design will not manufacture a before-and-after chart.

**5. Record — the complete public evidence index**

The sheets stand into three paired records. Each pairs an output with its status and attribution, so the visitor can assess the work without inferring ownership from a prominent title or number.

| Record | Information shown | Available interaction |
|---|---|---|
| **“Timing structure in the Vela array,” 2024** | Published consortium paper; 84 authors; your timing calibration and validation contribution. | Open the publication. |
| **“Reference-source calibration for modular detectors,” 2026** | Separate public preprint, under review and not accepted. Your specific contribution remains unspecified in the current material. | Open the preprint; enlarge approved figures with credits. |
| **ArrayTime** | Lab’s awarded €1.8m grant; your supervisor as principal investigator; your contribution was writing the calibration work-package section. | Read the contribution detail; follow a public grant page if its URL is supplied. |

The 3D index is accompanied by an ordinary linked text list. Titles, status and contribution remain readable without rotating a sheet.

This section receives slightly more scrolling space than the others because it contains the densest evidence.

**6. Handover — the conclusion and contact**

The sheets reunite into a complete protocol stack. An evidence index remains visible on its face, connecting the conclusion to the material just shown.

The closing explanation answers the opening question through your confirmed calibration and validation contribution, your working documents, and the limits of the evidence. Final wording will be written from those facts.

The visitor can:

- Download your CV.
- Email you.
- Revisit the publication index.
- Return to any chapter or the top.

The close states your fellowship and research instrumentation interests. It gives a hiring panel a straightforward next step.

**How the scrolling works**

On desktop, the story occupies roughly seven screens across six chapters. That is a starting proportion; readable content determines the final length.

The document object sits beside the text in a sticky scene. Scrolling changes sheet spacing, orientation and shallow camera position. Each transformation settles into a readable arrangement before the next begins.

Navigation uses native scrolling. Chapter links allow people to bypass transitions and jump directly to evidence. There is no forced snapping or timed sequence.

Sheet faces carry short labels and visual evidence. Paragraphs, citations and links remain in normal page text. The scene communicates relationships without becoming a reading obstacle.

**The look**

The chosen palette comes from the material of the object:

| Element | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Page background | Warm ivory, `#F3F0E8` |
| Main text | Graphite, `#202A2D` |
| Accent and links | Deep teal, `#096B63` |
| Document sheets | Matte cream, `#FFFCF5` |
| Depth | Fine sheet edges, restrained shadows and subtle separation |
| Graphic details | Thin rules, index numbers and precise alignment |

Approved schematics and preprint figures supply the visual specificity. Credits appear beside the assets.

**Source Sans 3** handles headings, paragraphs and navigation. **IBM Plex Mono** handles document labels, index numbers and technical notation. Fonts are self-hosted.

Body text starts around 18px on desktop and 17px on phones, with a comfortable reading width. Publication statuses use explicit words; colour is supplementary. Long text stays off moving textures.

**Phone, accessibility and fallback behavior**

| Situation | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| **Phone or narrow screen** | A single-column document with lightweight static sheet compositions between sections. The desktop scene and long scroll transitions are replaced by ordinary reading flow. |
| **Reduced motion** | Settled illustrations for each chapter, with immediate navigation and no camera travel, gathering animation or parallax. |
| **Unavailable or failed WebGL** | Static SVG/image arrangements showing the same relationships, followed by the complete text and links. |
| **JavaScript disabled** | The full HTML document, standard chapter anchors, publication links, CV download and email link. Figures link to their readable originals. |
| **Keyboard or screen reader** | Logical headings and reading order, a skip link, visible keyboard focus and meaningful figure descriptions. Essential information is available outside the canvas. |

On phones, publication status and attribution stay together. Diagrams open at a useful size, controls have at least 44px touch targets, and contact shortcuts do not cover the text. There is no horizontal scrolling or empty space reserved for disabled animations.

**Everything else the site needs**

“Include” below means part of a future implementation, not work being built now.

| Requirement | Scope |
|---|---|
| **Navigation** | Chapter anchors, active chapter indicator, skip link, publication shortcut and CV/contact links. |
| **Complete work index** | Both papers and the grant-writing contribution, with their distinctions intact. |
| **CV and email** | An accessible downloadable CV and a verified public email address. |
| **Figure handling** | Approved assets, exact credits, accessible descriptions and readable enlargement views. |
| **Publication upkeep** | Explicit status and a last-checked date in the content record; update the 2026 status only after confirmation. |
| **Search information** | Descriptive title, summary, semantic headings, canonical address and sitemap. |
| **Shared-link preview** | Your name, research contribution and a document-stack image. |
| **Site icon** | A simple sheet/index mark derived from the main object. |
| **404 page** | Clear links back to the portfolio, publications and contact. |
| **Performance** | Readable content loads first; optional 3D loads afterward. Compressed assets, small geometry and bounded rendering resolution. |
| **Privacy** | Self-hosted fonts and assets; no third-party tracking by default. |
| **Legal requirements** | Resolve any required notice using the actual jurisdiction and hosting arrangements before launch. |
| **Hosting and domain** | Static hosting is suitable; select these before a later authorized launch. |
| **Language** | English initially. |
| **Separate research pages** | Later, when substantial public evidence warrants deeper explanations. |
| **Blog** | Optional later addition if you want to maintain public writing. |
| **Testimonials, awards and chat** | Outside the initial scope. |

A future build should be checked on an ordinary phone, with keyboard navigation, reduced motion, disabled JavaScript and failed WebGL. Checks should also cover publication destinations, credits, CV accessibility, contact links, contrast and every personal claim against the fact sheet.

**Assumptions and remaining inputs**

I selected the protocol structure, warm-paper palette, typography and six-chapter order using your instruction to exercise judgment. The sheet contents are editorial summaries unless actual approved documents are supplied.

The remaining implementation inputs are the public email, CV file, publication URLs, chosen figures/schematics, their credits and descriptions. More detail about the residual comparison would support a richer evidence presentation, but the present plan can use the confirmed scoped statement.

The plan excludes raw consortium data and unpublished internal plots. It also leaves unconfirmed career history, document contents and individual ownership claims out of the story.

The full plan is saved in [storyboard.md](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-physicist-with-GtZ6NJ/docs/story/storyboard.md), with [source facts](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-physicist-with-GtZ6NJ/docs/story/facts.md) and [design decisions](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-physicist-with-GtZ6NJ/docs/story/decided-for-you.md). No website or prototype has been built.
